issue.title: Use-after-free in `itertools.groupby` via re-entrant key comparison through `__eq__`

labels.name: extension-modules
labels.description: C modules in the Modules dir

labels.name: type-crash
labels.description: A hard crash of the interpreter, possibly with a core dump

issue.body:
### What happened?

`groupby_next` compares the current and target keys with `PyObject_RichCompareBool` while holding pointers to the active key/value pair. A user-defined `__eq__` can call back into `next(groupby)` mid-compare, advancing the iterator, replacing `currkey/currvalue`, and dereferencing the objects still in use by the outer compare. The outer compare then dereferences freed memory, crashing in `_Py_IsImmortal`.

**Proof of Concept:**

```python
from itertools import groupby


class Key(bytearray):
    seen = False

    def __init__(self, is_first):
        self.is_first = is_first

    def __eq__(self, other):
        global G
        if self.is_first and not Key.seen:
            Key.seen = True
            next(G)
            return NotImplemented
        return False


def keys():
    yield Key(True)
    while True:
        yield Key(False)


G = groupby([None, 1], keys().send)
next(G)
next(G)
```

**Vulnerable Code Snippet:**

<details>
<summary>Click to expand</summary>

```c
/* Buggy Re-entrant Path */
static PyObject *
builtin_next(PyObject *self, PyObject *const *args, Py_ssize_t nargs)
{
    PyObject *it, *res;
    /* ... */
    it = args[0];
    res = (*Py_TYPE(it)->tp_iternext)(it);
    /* ... */
    return res;
}

static PyObject *
groupby_next(PyObject *op)
{
    PyObject *r, *grouper;
    groupbyobject *gbo = groupbyobject_CAST(op);

    gbo->currgrouper = NULL;
    /* skip to next iteration group */
    for (;;) {
        if (gbo->currkey == NULL)
            /* pass */;
        else if (gbo->tgtkey == NULL)
            break;
        else {
            int rcmp;

            rcmp = PyObject_RichCompareBool(gbo->tgtkey, gbo->currkey, Py_EQ);  /* crashing pointer derived */
            if (rcmp == -1)
                return NULL;
            else if (rcmp == 0)
                break;
        }

        if (groupby_step(gbo) < 0)
            return NULL;
    }
    Py_INCREF(gbo->currkey);
    Py_XSETREF(gbo->tgtkey, gbo->currkey);

    grouper = _grouper_create(gbo, gbo->tgtkey);
    if (grouper == NULL)
        return NULL;

    r = PyTuple_Pack(2, gbo->currkey, grouper);
    Py_DECREF(grouper);
    return r;
}

static PyObject *
slot_tp_richcompare(PyObject *self, PyObject *other, int op)
{
    PyObject *res = _PyObject_MaybeCallSpecialOneArg(self, name_op[op], other);  /* Reentrant call site */
    /* ... */
    return res;
}

static inline Py_ALWAYS_INLINE int _Py_IsImmortal(PyObject *op)
{
#if SIZEOF_VOID_P > 4
    return _Py_CAST(PY_INT32_T, op->ob_refcnt) < 0;  /* Crash site */
#else
    return op->ob_refcnt >= _Py_IMMORTAL_MINIMUM_REFCNT;
#endif
}

/* Clobbering Path */
Py_LOCAL_INLINE(int)
groupby_step(groupbyobject *gbo)
{
    PyObject *newvalue, *newkey, *oldvalue;
    /* ... */
    oldvalue = gbo->currvalue;
    gbo->currvalue = newvalue;
    Py_XSETREF(gbo->currkey, newkey);  /* state mutate site */
    Py_XDECREF(oldvalue);
    return 0;
}
```
</details>

comments.body:
Hi, I’m interested in working on this.

From the PoC, the crash appears to be caused by re-entrancy during
PyObject_RichCompareBool in groupby_next: while comparing keys,
a user-defined __eq__ can re-enter next(groupby), advancing the
iterator and invalidating the borrowed references to currkey /
currvalue that are still in use by the outer comparison.

My initial proposal is a minimal fix that ensures the objects
participating in the rich comparison remain alive for the duration
of the call (for example, by temporarily INCREFing the current and
target keys around PyObject_RichCompareBool), so that re-entrancy
cannot lead to use-after-free.

I wanted to check whether this approach matches maintainer
expectations, or if a different strategy (e.g. a re-entrancy guard)
would be preferred before I start implementing a patch.
Thank you @jackfromeast for the report, and @VanshAgarwal24036 for the fix!
